articles.headline: Week 3 winners and losers: Gibbs and JSN stay hot; St. Brown and Taylor go quiet
articles.description: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba came up big in Week 3, while Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor had very quiet days.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. On the flip side, fantasy stars Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown all had disappointing games.

Who were the big winners and losers around the league during the third week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 3

1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

He's sure proving worthy of that No. 1 overall fantasy pick, as he has scored at least 23 fantasy points in all three games, posted 75% snap and 78% rushing shares, and has totaled an easily position-best 98.3 points for the season. That latter number ranks 15th in history through three team games of any season. Isiah Pacheco's back and MCL injuries have locked Gibbs in as a three-down dynamo and the odds are good that Gibbs will maintain his positional lead in fantasy points for the duration of 2026. -- Cockcroft

2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, and Sam Darnold, QB, Seattle Seahawks

It's incredible to think that Smith-Njigba is off to the stellar start that he is despite Darnold's having missed the near-entirety of the first two due to injury and the team's running game having been only so-so thus far. Smith-Njigba scored 35.36 fantasy points, giving him 104.06 through three games, the fourth-most ever through that many by any player in history. Meanwhile Darnold committed a pair of interceptions in his return to the lineup, but he didn't seem at all slowed by the glute injury, finishing with 27.66 points of his own. Smith-Njigba's elite play should bring Darnold's fantasy utility up, and the two have a good matchup against a struggling Los Angeles Chargers team in Week 4, before hitting a tougher stretch of their 2026 schedule (SF, @DEN, KC, from Weeks 5-7). -- Cockcroft

3. Joe Burrow, QB, and Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

In the Week 3 loss to the Steelers, Burrow notched his best numbers of the season, completing 75.7% of his throws for 282 yards and three touchdowns, plus he rushed for 13 yards (22.58 points). Chase caught nine of a team-high 12 targets for 98 yards and a score (24.8 points). That gives Chase two straight games of 24 or more points after that rough opening week. Chase will remain a top-3 play at wide receiver for Week 4, while Burrow -- who has thrown for at least two touchdowns in back-to-back games -- will be a lower-tier QB1 in my ranks. ---Bowen

4. Geno Smith, QB, Garrett Wilson, WR, and Kenyon Sadiq, TE, New York Jets

In a positive matchup versus the Detroit secondary, Smith scored a season-best 26.04 points, throwing for 321 yards and four touchdowns. articles.headline: Several Panthers starters banged up in loss to Browns
articles.description: The Panthers lost to the Browns 21-18 on Sunday, and they might have lost a few starters, at least temporarily, to injury in the defeat.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Carolina Panthers lost 21-18 to the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, and they might have lost a few starters, at least temporarily, to injury as well.

Quarterback Bryce Young (lower body), cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin), left guard Damien Lewis (elbow) and wide receiver Jalen Coker (quad) left the game during various points because of injuries.

Young and Lewis, who were inspected by trainers, both returned to the field in the second half.

Following the game, coach Dave Canales said Young was dealing with "something." When asked whether the injury was related to Young's lower body, Canales affirmed the location.

"He's working through something, but he was able to finish," Canales said. "We'll give you more information on that once we get a full evaluation. But he was cleared to go back in and finish the game.

"There [were] a couple of balls that he would normally hit, so I'm wondering if he was working through something -- trying to find his base to get those balls off. He can make those throws, from different platforms and different things. He'd be the first one to tell you that up here. But he settled in, he found a way to play ball, and all of a sudden, we're moving the chains again and really just proud of how he battled us back right into the game."

Young, who threw for 291 yards, a touchdown and an interception against Cleveland, didn't make excuses for coming up short against the Browns. He also wouldn't provide detail on his ailment.

"Nothing -- it's football; we're all dealing with stuff," Young said. "It doesn't have any bearing on the game. Tough one, just didn't get it done."

Carolina was already without linebacker Devin Lloyd (calf), wide receiver Xavier Legette (knee) and safety Nick Scott (rib) entering the game.

Coker, who had been battling an ankle injury, played throughout the first half but left with a quad injury.

"His quad lit up on him a little bit," Canales said. "And so, the pain wasn't really going away. We're testing the strength, and we decided we couldn't put him back out there in that condition."

Jackson also left the game in the first half. Horn exited after the game-winning touchdown throw from Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson to tight end Harold Fannin Jr.

"We're going to have to evaluate that and see where he's at," Canales said of Horn. "But he was not going to be coming back in."

The Panthers will host the Detroit Lions (2-1) on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 4. They'll then have a bye in Week 5.

Longtime starting tackles Taylor Moton (blood clot) and Ickey Ekwonu (patellar tendon) are eligible to return from the non-football injury list and physically unable to perform list, respectively, following the bye. Defensive end Tershawn Wharton is also eligible to return from the PUP list for Week 6.

articles.headline: Trevor Lawrence explains kneel at the 1-yard line -- and what it means for fantasy owners
articles.description: The quarterback laughed off his clock-killing blunder, acknowledging the obvious fantasy implications after he knelt instead of walking into the end zone.
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Trevor Lawrence lost track of time, and as a result some fantasy football owners lost six points.

Lawrence took a knee at the 1-yard line on a scramble with nearly nine minutes remaining in the Jacksonville Jaguars' victory over the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon. The Jaguars were leading 28-6 at the time, so his decision was confusing because they didn't need to run more time off the clock to ensure their victory.

And then running back Bhayshul Tuten scored on the next play, which meant Tuten's fantasy owners ended up with six points instead.

Lawrence good-naturedly owned up to his goof after the game, which the Jaguars won 35-6 at EverBank Stadium.

"When I broke free and no one tackled me, it's something we talk about all the time potentially in those situations, going down, keeping the clock running," Lawrence said. "That was too much time. I looked at the clock after and I was like ugh, there's still eight minutes left. Probably unnecessary there, but just trying to eat as much clock is possible, trying to give them as few chances as possible to get back in the game.

"If you do the analytics, people will probably be all over it online, I'm sure. Probably wasn't the best decision, but we scored the next play. Give Bhayshul a touchdown. That's cool. Let him get in the end zone."

That was the only thing head coach Liam Coen could think was running through his quarterback's mind.

"I think he wanted to give a touchdown to somebody else," Coen joked after the game.

Lawrence said he doesn't remember Coen saying anything to him after the play or on the sideline after Tuten's touchdown run. But his teammates certainly were talking.

"Everybody's just kind of making fun of me," he said. "So yeah, maybe overthought that one just a little bit."

articles.headline: Vikings rule out Justin Jefferson with ankle injury
articles.description: Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after a first-quarter injury to his left ankle.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングス、足首負傷でジャスティン・ジェファーソンの途中離脱を発表
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスのスターレシーバー、ジャスティン・ジェファーソンは、日曜日のタンパベイ・バッカニアーズ戦の第1クォーターで左足首を負傷し、途中離脱となった。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Minnesota Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after suffering a first-quarter injury to his left ankle.

The injury appeared to occur on the Vikings' final offensive play of their first possession, at the end of a 10-yard catch on a screen pass. Jefferson had caught a 22-yard pass earlier on the drive.

Jefferson never required medical assistance on the field but eventually had an extended visit in the medical tent. He emerged in the second quarter wearing his helmet and then watched the game from the sideline for a while before walking to the locker room. He was not seen on the sideline in the second half of the game.

In his absence, the Vikings shifted their offensive focus to No. 2 receiver Jordan Addison, who caught a 41-yard pass from Kyler Murray to give the team a 17-10 lead with 4:11 remaining in the second quarter. Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton were the Vikings' other receivers when they used three-receiver sets.

Jefferson has largely been healthy in his NFL career, playing in every Vikings game in five of his six full seasons. The exception was a torn right hamstring in 2023, an injury that cost him seven games before he was able to return.

He had the worst season of his career in 2025 as the Vikings tried to transition to quarterback J.J. McCarthy while also using rookie Max Brosmer for two starts. Jefferson finished with 1,048 receiving yards for the season. That total in 17 games was less than he accumulated during his 10-game stint in 2023.

The Vikings' decision to replace McCarthy with Murray brought hope that Jefferson could resume his explosive production. He caught eight passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1, mostly from backup Carson Wentz after Murray sustained a concussion but managed only three catches for 55 yards in a rain-soaked Week 2 game at the Chicago Bears.

Jefferson's 179 receiving yards this season is the fewest he has had through three weeks in his career.

articles.headline: Harbaugh says Winston is QB1 even if Giants add another QB
articles.description: Jameis Winston will remain the Giants' starting quarterback even if a quarterback is added in the coming days, coach John Harbaugh said Sunday.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Jameis Winston threw for 119 yards in a steady rain and the New York Giants didn't get into the end zone in his first start in place of the injured Jaxson Dart. It was enough to lead his team to a 12-7 victory and keep the starting job, no matter whom they add at the position in the coming days.

"Yes. Yes, I do," coach John Harbaugh said definitively on whether he believes Winston will remain the team's starter. "Yes, I do."

Dart is out for at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing knee surgery Friday. Winston took over early in last Monday night's loss to the Los Angeles Rams and struggled.

Winston and Harbaugh said he did what was "required" on Sunday in the difficult conditions against the Titans. That meant leading the Giants on four scoring drives and not turning the ball over in the wet and windy weather as a result of a nor'easter.

It didn't seem to be a differentiator one way or another. The Giants insist how Winston played isn't affecting the current starting quarterback situation.

"Not at all," Harbaugh said. "Not at all. The plans are the plans. The opportunities that you have are the opportunities you have. No matter what, we're going to do everything we can to make our team as strong as we can based on what options we have."

New York (2-1) hosts the Arizona Cardinals next week at MetLife Stadium. It still remains likely the Giants will have a new quarterback on the roster this week.

The inexperienced Jake Haener served as Winston's backup Sunday.

The Giants are expected to add a quarterback in the coming days with free agent Jimmy Garappolo, Arizona's Gardner Minshew II and Minnesota's J.J. McCarthy among the options, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

"I'm not worried about that. I don't care about that," offensive tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said. "Jameis is our quarterback now. We're going to ride with him for the rest of the season."

The goal is to win games. The Giants did that Sunday, when they never trailed.

Winston has the support and trust of the locker room.

"Yeah, I mean, we did win, didn't we? We trust our guy back there," center John Michael Schmitz said. "We trust that he can get the job done. We've got all the belief in him as our quarterback."

Winston, a 12-year veteran, isn't paying much attention to the outside noise. He has been around long enough to understand how this all works.

The veteran quarterback earned his first win in three starts for the Giants dating back to his signing with the team before the start of last season.

"Y'all ask me: How does it feel to win your first game as a New York Giants starting quarterback? That's the stuff I choose to focus on: the seed of good in everything," Winston said.

articles.headline: 49ers rule veteran WR Mike Evans out after rib injury
articles.description: The 49ers lost veteran WR Mike Evans in the first half of Sunday's game against the Cardinals due to a rib injury.
articles.headlineJa: 49ers、肋骨負傷のベテランWRマイク・エバンスの離脱を発表
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersのベテランWRマイク・エバンスは、日曜日のカーディナルス戦前半に肋骨を負傷して途中離脱した。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The injuries continue to mount for the San Francisco 49ers as receiver Mike Evans departed in the first half of Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.

It was unclear exactly what happened to Evans, but he was slow to come off the field after a third-down pass from quarterback Brock Purdy intended for him over the middle fell incomplete. A few plays earlier, he got hit on the sternum during a completion over the middle but stayed in for a couple of snaps before departing.

Niners medical staff ran onto the field and helped Evans as he clutched at the right side of his sternum. Evans got up slowly and walked to the sideline where he entered the medical tent and, after a few minutes, got on a cart to go to the locker room.

At halftime, the Niners ruled out his return due to a rib injury. Evans, who managed a hip injury during the week, finished his day with three catches for 34 yards and a touchdown.

Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, meanwhile, departed to be evaluated for concussion earlier in the half. He cleared that evaluation and returned to the game on Arizona's first possession of the third quarter.

articles.headline: Parma part ways with ex-Arsenal assistant Carlos Cuesta
articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
